charts.title: Lifting the discrete events into vivarium reproduces the full model (hybrid vs full, 6 observables)
charts.caption: The event-free SBML core run by Tellurium, with the infection (E_infect) and TLR hysteresis (E_tlrOn/Off) lifted out of the model into general viva-impulse Steps (a ScheduledEvent and a ThresholdSwitch) coupled through TelluriumImpulseBridge, reproduces the full event-driven model (same proto_valve continuous core, events relocated): hemodynamics to ~1e-03 relative, blood pathogen to 20.4%. The residual is the tick-quantization of the infection timing — the ScheduledEvent fires at the first 10 s tick >= infectionStart, vs the SBML event's exact root-find. The discrete events are now explicit, inspectable and swappable at the composite level without editing the SBML.

charts.title: Event-driven simulator vs the other run options — runtime and predictions
charts.caption: The event-driven hybrid (event-free SBML core + viva-impulse ScheduledEvent/ThresholdSwitch) against the other run options. Runtime (same roadrunner engine + Composite harness, this machine, 2 h severity-3): full sepsis_sbml 284 s, proto_valve 236 s, hybrid 233 s — the hybrid matches the fastest exact option and is 1.22x faster than the full event-driven model, because its continuous core is event-free (no CVODE root returns) and the lifted events are cheap. Predictions: it REPRODUCES the exact engine — hemodynamics to ~1e-4 relative, immune core essentially exact; the one larger figure (blood pathogen, ~20% peak) is a brief transient from the tick-quantized infection start, converging to ~0.2%. Unlike the learned surrogate (study 04: ~1000x faster but inadmissible on 8/9 severe observables), the event-driven format buys explicit, swappable events at no fidelity or runtime cost versus the fastest exact engine.
